calls.reason: Gonen and colleagues measure semantic leakage in completions, but do not show how many factual hallucinations it causes. The evidence establishes the phenomenon without establishing the claimed prevalence.

The Gonen and Chen studies demonstrate irrelevant associations influencing outputs, but neither distinguishes word associations from concept-level processing. That central part of the claim remains unclear.

Betley documents vulnerabilities, while Wanner reports effective mitigations for studied examples. Neither settles whether comprehensive patching will ever be possible; the open-ended, partly hedged forecast remains uncallable.

Roh and colleagues report that phonetic lyric rewrites bypass Suno's filters and produce strong melodic and rhythmic resemblance to identified songs. Their pre-post study directly supports the demonstrated bypass.
